facts.value: The term engineering is derived from the word engineer, which dates back to the 14th century when an engine'er referred to 'a constructor of military engines'.
facts.programme_association: Engineering Management Master's Emphasis | ASU Online

facts.value: In this context, an 'engine' referred to a military machine, such as a catapult.
facts.programme_association: Engineering Management Master's Emphasis | ASU Online

facts.value: The term civil engineering entered the lexicon to distinguish between those specializing in the construction of non-military projects and those involved in military engineering.
facts.programme_association: Engineering Management Master's Emphasis | ASU Online

facts.value: The word 'engine' ultimately derives from the Latin ingenium, meaning 'innate quality, especially mental power, hence a clever invention.'
